data.text:
## menu — Menu (component, archetype navigate)
A transient list of choices or commands revealed from a trigger.
Aliases: dropdown menu, context menu, overflow menu, menu bar, mega menu
Anatomy: Trigger (What opens the menu); Items (Choices and commands); Structure (Sections and submenus)
Related — neighbors: command-palette, popover
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Opening [invocation] — What opens it?
  - openBy (single-select: one id) — Opened by
      button-click: Button click (e.g. Overflow ⋮ menus)
      right-click-or-long-press: Right-click or long-press (e.g. Context menus)
      menu-bar: Menu bar (e.g. macOS menu bar)
      hover: Hover (e.g. Retail mega menus)
      keyboard: Keyboard (e.g. Alt to reach Windows menus)
* Structure [composition] — How are items organized?
  - structure (single-select: one id) — Structure
      flat: Flat (e.g. Overflow menus)
      sections: Sections (e.g. Google Docs menus)
      cascading-submenus: Cascading submenus (e.g. Desktop menu bars)
      mega-menu: Mega menu — Multi-column panel (e.g. Retail department menus)
* Item content [content] — What does each item show?
  - item (multi-select: list of ids) — Item content
      label: Label (e.g. All)
      icon: Icon (e.g. Google Docs)
      shortcut-hint: Shortcut hint (e.g. macOS menus)
      checkmark-state: Checkmark state (e.g. View menus)
      description: Description (e.g. GitHub menus)
* Item set [initiative] — Who decides which items appear and in what order?
  - itemSet (single-select: one id) — Item set
      fixed: Fixed (e.g. Most menus)
      depends-on-selection: Depends on selection (e.g. Context menus)
      adaptive: Adaptive — The system reorders by use (e.g. Office 2000 personalized menus)
      adaptable: Adaptable — The person reorders (e.g. Office Quick Access Toolbar)
* Form [layout] — What shape is it?
  - form (single-select: one id) — Form
      vertical-list: Vertical list (e.g. Most menus)
      radial: Radial (e.g. Blender pie menus)
      icon-grid: Icon grid (e.g. Google apps launcher)
      horizontal-bar: Horizontal bar (e.g. Toolbars)

## drawer — Drawer (component, archetype navigate)
A panel that slides in from a screen edge, holding navigation, detail, filters or an assistant beside the main content.
Aliases: side sheet, flyout panel, slide-over
Anatomy: Panel (The drawer surface); Scrim (What covers content when modal); Handle or trigger (What opens it)
Related — neighbors: modal-dialog, bottom-sheet, split-pane
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Edge and relationship [layout] — Which edge, and does it cover, push or sit beside content?
  - edge (single-select: one id) — Edge
      left: Left (e.g. Navigation drawers)
      right: Right (e.g. Detail panels)
      top: Top (e.g. Notification shades)
  - relationship (single-select: one id) — Relationship to content
      overlay-with-scrim: Overlay with scrim (e.g. Material modal navigation drawer)
      push-content: Push content (e.g. Standard drawers)
      docked: Docked (e.g. Material standard side sheet)
      overlay-no-scrim: Overlay, no scrim — The panel lies over the content without dimming or disabling it visually (GitHub Projects item panel, Notion side peek, OS panels) (e.g. GitHub Projects — Item side panel)
* Contents [content] — What is it for?
  - holds (single-select: one id) — Holds
      navigation: Navigation (e.g. Gmail on Android)
      item-detail: Item detail (e.g. GitHub Projects item panel)
      filters: Filters (e.g. Mobile retail)
      settings: Settings (e.g. Admin consoles)
      assistant: Assistant (e.g. Microsoft Edge Copilot sidebar)
      system-status-and-controls: System status and controls — Notifications, quick toggles and widgets belonging to the OS rather than the app (Android shade, iOS Control Center, Windows Widgets, macOS Notification Center) (e.g. Android — Notification shade)
      companion-apps: Companion apps — Small versions of ot

## chat-thread — Chat thread (pattern, archetype communicate)
A chronological sequence of messages between participants, with a composer at the edge.
Aliases: messaging view, conversation, DM
Anatomy: Message list (The history); Message (One turn); Composer (Writing the next turn); Header (Participants and actions)
Related — uses: reactions, text-field, file-upload, badge, autocomplete | specializes: communicate | neighbors: comment-thread, ai-chat, feed
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Message layout [layout] — How are messages drawn?
  - layout (single-select: one id) — Layout
      bubbles-by-sender: Bubbles by sender (e.g. iMessage)
      stream-with-avatars: Stream with avatars (e.g. Slack)
      compact-lines: Compact lines (e.g. Discord compact mode)
      cozy: Cozy (e.g. Discord cozy mode)
* Reply structure [composition] — How do replies relate to messages?
  - replies (single-select: one id) — Replies
      flat: Flat (e.g. SMS)
      quoted-inline-replies: Quoted inline replies (e.g. WhatsApp replies)
      side-threads: Side threads (e.g. Slack threads)
      topic-threads: Topic threads (e.g. Zulip)
* Message content [content] — What can a message carry, and what metadata shows?
  - content (multi-select: list of ids) — Content
      text: Text (e.g. All)
      media-and-files: Media and files (e.g. All)
      link-previews: Link previews (e.g. iMessage)
      interactive-cards: Interactive cards (e.g. Slack Block Kit)
      voice-messages: Voice messages (e.g. WhatsApp)
  - metadata (multi-select: list of ids) — Metadata
      timestamp: Timestamp (e.g. All)
      read-receipts: Read receipts (e.g. WhatsApp)
      edited-marker: Edited marker (e.g. Slack)
      delivery-status: Delivery status (e.g. Signal)
* Message lifetime [lifecycle] — What happens to a message over time?
  - lifetime (single-select: one id) — Lifetime
      permanent: Permanent (e.g. SMS)
      editable-and-deletable: Editable and deletable (e.g. Slack)
      disappearing: Disappearing (e.g. Signal disappearing messages)
      scheduled-send: Scheduled send (e.g. Slack scheduled messages)
* Composer actions [invocation] — What can be done from the composer?
  - composer (multi-select: list of ids) — Composer
      send-on-enter: Send on Enter (e.g. Desktop chat)
      slash-commands: Slash commands (e.g. Slack)
      mentions: Mentions (e.g. @ in Slack)
      attachments: Attachments (e.g. All)
      formatting-toolbar: Formatting toolbar (e.g. Slack)
* Unread position [feedback] — Where does a returning reader land?
  - unread (single-select: one id) — Unread
      latest-message: Latest message (e.g. WhatsApp)
      new-messages-divider: New messages divider (e.g. Slack)
      first-unread: First unread (e.g. Discord)

## chart — Chart (pattern, archetype analyze)
A visual encoding of data values as marks and channels so a person can see distributions, comparisons and trends.
Aliases: plot, graph, visualization
Anatomy: Marks (The visual elements); Axes and scales (How values map to space); Legend (How channels are decoded); Tooltip (Detail on demand for a mark); Controls (Encoding and filter affordances)
Related — uses: tooltip, filter-controls, stat-tile | specializes: analyze | neighbors: coordinated-views, pivot-table, dashboard

* Mark encoding [encoding] — What marks and channels carry the data?
  - markType (single-select: one id) — Mark type
      points: Points (e.g. Scatterplots)
      bars: Bars (e.g. Bar charts)
      lines: Lines (e.g. Line charts)
      areas: Areas (e.g. Area charts)
      arcs: Arcs (e.g. Pie and donut)

      length: Length (e.g. Bars)

data.text:
## task-list — Task list (pattern, archetype schedule)
Ordered or grouped actionable items with completion state, often carrying due dates, assignees and priority without requiring a full time grid.
Aliases: to-do list, checklist, task manager, action list
Anatomy: List (The ordered or grouped set of tasks); Task row (Title plus key attributes); Completion control (Check, done or status); Detail (Fuller fields for one task)
Related — uses: choice-control, date-picker, filter-controls, drag-reorder, inline-edit, empty-state | specializes: schedule | neighbors: calendar, gantt-timeline, kanban-board, inbox
Dimensions (dims key = sub-dimension id; values = value ids):
* Task representation [content] — What does each row show, and how rich is the item?
  - rowFields (multi-select: list of ids) — Row fields
      title-only: Title only (e.g. Classic paper-like lists)
      due-date: Due date (e.g. Apple Reminders)
      assignee: Assignee (e.g. Asana list)
      priority-or-score: Priority or score (e.g. Todoist priority flags)
      project-or-tags: Project or tags (e.g. Todoist labels)
      sub-task-progress: Sub-task progress (e.g. Things checklist progress)
      estimate: Estimate (e.g. Linear estimate)
  - itemRichness (single-select: one id) — Item richness
      checkbox-item: Checkbox item — Little more than done + title (e.g. Apple Reminders)
      issue-like-task: Issue-like task — Description, comments, fields (e.g. Linear)
      checklist-inside-a-doc: Checklist inside a doc — Tasks embedded in prose (e.g. Notion to-do blocks)
      recurring-template: Recurring template — Repeats on a rule (e.g. Todoist recurring)
* Ordering and grouping [composition] — What structure holds the tasks?
  - taskStructure (single-select: one id) — Structure
      manual-order: Manual order — Drag to prioritize (e.g. Things Today)
      grouped-by-date: Grouped by date — Overdue / Today / Upcoming (e.g. Todoist)
      grouped-by-project-or-list: Grouped by project or list (e.g. Apple Reminders lists)
      grouped-by-assignee-or-status: Grouped by assignee or status (e.g. Asana)
      hierarchical-outline: Hierarchical outline — Indent for sub-tasks (e.g. Workflowy, Dynalist)
      filter-defined-smart-list: Filter-defined smart list — Saved query as a list (e.g. Todoist filters)
* Scheduling link [encoding] — How does the list connect to clock time?
  - timeBinding (single-select: one id) — Time binding
      no-dates: No dates — Pure ordered work (e.g. Simple checklists)
      due-date-only: Due date only — Day without time (e.g. Many to-do apps)
      due-date-and-time: Due date and time (e.g. Google Tasks with time)
      time-block-on-calendar: Time block on calendar — Task appears as a calendar event (e.g. Motion, Reclaim)
      deadline-plus-soft-plan-date: Deadline plus soft plan date — Separate plan vs due (e.g. Things deadlines vs when)
* Completing and triaging [flow] — How do tasks move toward done or deferral?
  - completionPath (multi-select: list of ids) — Completion path
      check-off: Check off (e.g. Reminders)
      status-workflow: Status workflow — Todo → In progress → Done (e.g. Linear)
      snooze-defer: Snooze / defer — Leave incomplete but hide until later (e.g. Things Tonight / Anytime)
      migrate-to-another-day: Migrate to another day — Roll unfinished forward (e.g. Bullet journal digital apps)
      convert-to-event-or-issue: Convert to event or issue (e.g. Slack save for later → reminders)
* Creation and detail [invocation] — How are tasks added and opened?
  - createOpen (multi-select: list of ids) — Create and open
      inline-add-row: Inline add row (e.g. Todoist)
      quick-add-shortcut: Quick-add shortcut (e.g. Todoist q)
      natural-language-parse: Natural language parse — “Email Sam tomorrow 5pm” (e.g. Todoist quick add)
      open-detail-pane: Open detail pane (e.g. Asana task pane)
      open-full-page: Open full page (e.g. Notion task pages)
      save-from-elsewhere: Save from elsewhere —

aesthetics.typography: Inter Variable for everything (display headings, nav, body, UI mockups); Berkeley Mono for small uppercase captions (FIG 0.1, 'Powering the companies...', changelog dates, TECH SPECS) and code in the diff mockup
aesthetics.typeScale: Strong contrast: 64px H1 with tight negative tracking, 48px section H2s (two-line, medium weight), 24px lead paragraphs, 15/14/13px UI and body text, 10-12px mono captions; weights mostly 400-510, hierarchy by size and gray value rather than bold

label.notes: Near-black (#08090a) canvas with product mockups rendered as live DOM (not images): panels fade into the background via edge gradients and vignettes so the UI seems to emerge from darkness; a silver radial glow sits under the hero mockup. Text hierarchy is carried by gray steps (#f7f8f8 > #d0d6e0 > #8a8f98 > #62666d) instead of weight. Section headings use a two-line split ('Intake / and integrations') left with a 24px paragraph right and a quiet 'Learn more ->'. Manifesto headline uses two-tone white+gray emphasis. Thin 1px dividers separate full-width chapters. Only saturated color comes from mockup status icons, teal scatter points, and the neon-yellow Ramp testimonial card that breaks the monochrome near the end. Pills (9999px) for nav CTA and CTA buttons; 8-12px radii on panels. Many depicted patterns (kanban, gantt, chat, agent run, diff) are illustrative product mockups with partial interactivity (e.g. editable diff textbox, Theme combobox), coded present with moderate confidence. Feature '+' triggers open a right drawer with TECH SPECS detail.

aesthetics.typography: Inter Variable for everything (display headings, nav, body, UI mockups); Berkeley Mono for small uppercase captions (FIG 0.1, 'Powering the companies...', changelog dates, TECH SPECS) and code in the diff mockup
aesthetics.typeScale: Strong contrast: 64px H1 with tight negative tracking, 48px section H2s (two-line, medium weight), 24px lead paragraphs, 15/14/13px UI and body text, 10-12px mono captions; weights mostly 400-510, hierarchy by size and gray value rather than bold

label.notes: Near-black (#08090a) canvas with product mockups rendered as live DOM (not images): panels fade into the background via edge gradients and vignettes so the UI seems to emerge from darkness; a silver radial glow sits under the hero mockup. Text hierarchy is carried by gray steps (#f7f8f8 > #d0d6e0 > #8a8f98 > #62666d) instead of weight. Section headings use a two-line split ('Intake / and integrations') left with a 24px paragraph right and a quiet 'Learn more ->'. Manifesto headline uses two-tone white+gray emphasis. Thin 1px dividers separate full-width chapters. Only saturated color comes from mockup status icons, teal scatter points, and the neon-yellow Ramp testimonial card that breaks the monochrome near the end. Pills (9999px) for nav CTA and CTA buttons; 8-12px radii on panels. Many depicted patterns (kanban, gantt, chat, agent run, diff) are illustrative product mockups with partial interactivity (e.g. editable diff textbox, Theme combobox), coded present with moderate confidence. Feature '+' triggers open a right drawer with TECH SPECS detail.
